fixer.summary: Magic Missile rolled each dart's d4 inline without going through the shared Heroic Inspiration reroll (d20.inspiration_reroll, which T-118 introduced). Now `_magic_missile` in dungdra/spells.py rolls one target's dart d4s as a group and passes them to inspiration_reroll(game, c.caster, rolls, 4). That offers the 'inspiration_damage' choice, rerolls the chosen die, spends the inspiration and logs it with rule GLOSS.heroic-inspiration#1 on page 183. Damage is then the sum of (d4+1) per dart. The code is tagged SRD[GLOSS.heroic-inspiration#1]. I added three unit tests: a reroll that spends inspiration, no reroll without inspiration, and a Shield-warded target that takes no damage, rolls no dice and keeps the caster's inspiration. The third test covers the Shield branch so the dev-gate coverage ratchet doesn't fall. Checks: tests/unit has 572 passing. The ticket test passes with --runxfail. Without --runxfail it shows as a strict XPASS failure, which goes away when the harness removes the marker. The rest of tests/srd and tests/scenarios pass. ruff check and ruff format --check are clean, and the dev-gate passes with coverage at 50.67%, up from 50.66%.

review.summary: Magic Missile now rolls each target's dart d4s and passes them through the existing shared `inspiration_reroll` helper, the same one used for weapon damage and Hit Dice, before damage is dealt. This adds no second mechanism. Under R-47 one die is rerolled and the others stand, and the new roll must be used. The log cites page=183 and rule=GLOSS.heroic-inspiration#1. The strict xfail on the acceptance test is removed and the test now passes, so the ticket's behaviour is fixed. The unit tests check behaviour: the damage total after rerolling a chosen dart, Inspiration being spent and its log rule, no reroll offered without Inspiration, and a Shielded target, where no dice are rolled, leaving Inspiration unspent. Nothing is hard-coded, out of layer or out of scope. The inline d20 reroll path is already covered by T-123.
